propositions: Canonical and legacy bridge status commands must expose identical read-only facts with identical exit codes and verdicts (HEALTHY/PAUSED/RUNNING/STALE/FOREIGN/NEVER_RUN/FAILED) without mutation, storing a single authoritative JSON record in refs/reconciler/last-pass before lock release with bounded three-attempt CAS and 100/200 ms backoff.

Process finalizer must write minimal durable last-pass JSON (schema version, pass id, environment id, outcome, failure kind, completion time, observed fence) via force-with-lease CAS, releasing the heartbeat during CAS then lock on success or failure, never claiming durability on exhausted contention or push/network/permission failure.

Status derives stable local identity from explicit REBAR_ENV_ID or local:<repo-env-id> from .env-id, treating missing/empty/unreadable .env-id as hard configuration error; LEGACY_JIRA_ENV_ID=reconciler, inbound event metadata, and old projections remain unchanged.

Canary fetches refs/reconciler/*, targets reconciler environment, performs two read-only live-lock snapshots across observed lease_secs (default 120, reject over 480s immediately), and detects CRASHED via unchanged OID/fence without heartbeat API query on the canonical github-api source=status path.

Rich detail file .bridge_state/last-pass.json is one rolling overwrite with diagnosis-only safety degradation when absent/stale/mismatched; matching success/failure/pause/RUNNING use live snapshot facts and lease; status never calls steal() or sleeps for lease.

ADR 0094 documents the authoritative ref, rolling detail, write-before-release, stalled-fence witness, rejected timestamp/accumulation alternatives, and extends ADR 0031 live-fence/lease-blob/CAS-classifier; numbering follows current convention with .numbers/0094, generated index, and both checker commands passing.
